[Christopher Eisgruber](/wiki/Christopher_L._Eisgruber "Christopher L. Eisgruber"), the 20th and current president of the university

Princeton's 20th and current president is Christopher Eisgruber, who was appointed by the university's [board of trustees](/wiki/Trustees_of_Princeton_University "Trustees of Princeton University") in 2013.[[134]](#cite_note-Yee-2013-136) The board is responsible for the overall direction of the university. It consists of no fewer than 23 and no more than 40 members at any one time, with the president of the university and the [governor of New Jersey](/wiki/Governor_of_New_Jersey "Governor of New Jersey") serving as [ex officio members](/wiki/Ex_officio_member "Ex officio member"). It approves the operating and capital budgets, supervises the investment of the university's endowment, and oversees campus real estate and long-range physical planning. The trustees also exercise prior review and approval concerning changes in major policies such as those in instructional programs and admission as well as tuition and fees and the hiring of faculty members.[[230]](#cite_note-233)

Earth's rotation period relative to the Sun—its mean solar day—is 86,400 seconds of mean solar time (86,400.0025 [SI](/wiki/SI "SI") seconds).[[184]](#cite_note-aj136_5_1906-193) Because Earth's solar day is now slightly longer than it was during the 19th century due to [tidal deceleration](/wiki/Tidal_acceleration "Tidal acceleration"), each day varies between 0 and 2 [ms](/wiki/Millisecond "Millisecond") longer than the mean solar day.[[185]](#cite_note-USNO_TSD-194)[[186]](#cite_note-195)

Earth's rotation period relative to the [fixed stars](/wiki/Fixed_star "Fixed star"), called its *stellar day* by the [International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service](/wiki/International_Earth_Rotation_and_Reference_Systems_Service "International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service") (IERS), is 86,164.0989 seconds of mean solar time ([UT1](/wiki/UT1 "UT1")), or 23h 56m 4.0989s.[[2]](#cite_note-IERS-4)[[n 10]](#cite_note-Aoki-196) Earth's rotation period relative to the [precessing](/wiki/Precession_(astronomy) "Precession (astronomy)") or moving mean [March equinox](/wiki/March_equinox "March equinox") (when the Sun is at 90° on the equator), is 86,164.0905 seconds of mean solar time (UT1) (23h 56m 4.0905s).[[2]](#cite_note-IERS-4) Thus the sidereal day is shorter than the stellar day by about 8.4 ms.[[187]](#cite_note-seidelmann1992-197)

Shaikh Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, the King of Bahrain

Bahrain is a [semi-constitutional monarchy](/wiki/Semi-constitutional_monarchy "Semi-constitutional monarchy") headed by King Shaikh Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. King Hamad enjoys wide executive powers which include appointing the [prime minister](/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Bahrain "Prime Minister of Bahrain") and his [ministers](/wiki/Cabinet_of_Bahrain "Cabinet of Bahrain"), commanding the Bahrain Defence Force, chairing the [Higher Judicial Council](/wiki/Judiciary_of_Bahrain "Judiciary of Bahrain"), appointing the [parliament](/wiki/National_Assembly_(Bahrain) "National Assembly (Bahrain)")'s [upper house](/wiki/Consultative_Council_(Bahrain) "Consultative Council (Bahrain)") and dissolving its elected [lower house](/wiki/Council_of_Representatives_(Bahrain) "Council of Representatives (Bahrain)").[[158]](#cite_note-:2-160) The head of government is the prime minister. In 2010, about half of [the cabinet](/wiki/Cabinet_of_Bahrain "Cabinet of Bahrain") was composed of the [Al Khalifa family](/wiki/House_of_Khalifa "House of Khalifa").[[159]](#cite_note-161)

Bahrain has a [bicameral](/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") National Assembly (*al-Majlis al-Watani*) consisting of the Shura Council (*Majlis Al-Shura*) with 40 seats and the Council of Representatives (*Majlis Al-Nuwab*) with 40 seats. The forty members of the Shura are appointed by the king. In the Council of Representatives, 40 members are elected by absolute majority vote in [gerrymandered](/wiki/Gerrymandered "Gerrymandered") single-member constituencies to serve four-year terms.[[160]](#cite_note-162) The appointed council "exercises a *de facto* veto" over the "rubber-stamp" elected, because draft acts must be approved so they may pass into law. The ex-king in 1818

Following Napoleon's deposing of the Bourbon dynasty, the ex-King, his wife, and former prime minister Godoy were held captive in France first at the [château de Compiègne](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Compi%C3%A8gne "Château de Compiègne")[[25]](#cite_note-25) and three years in [Marseille](/wiki/Marseille "Marseille") (where a neighborhood was named after him).[[26]](#cite_note-26) After the collapse of the regime installed by Napoleon, [Ferdinand VII](/wiki/Ferdinand_VII "Ferdinand VII") was restored to the throne. The former Charles IV drifted about Europe[[27]](#cite_note-Griffin-27) until 1812, when he finally settled in [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome"), in the [Palazzo Barberini](/wiki/Palazzo_Barberini "Palazzo Barberini").[[28]](#cite_note-WP-fr-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) His wife died on 2 January 1819, followed shortly by Charles, who died on 19 January of the same year. At the time of his death Charles was visiting his brother [Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies](/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_the_Two_Sicilies "Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies") in Naples.[[32]](#cite_note-32) Sir [Francis Ronalds](/wiki/Francis_Ronalds "Francis Ronalds") included a detailed description of the funeral in his travel journal.[[33]](#cite_note-33)[[34]](#cite_note-34)

Well-meaning and pious, Charles IV floundered in a series of international crises beyond his capacity to handle.[[27]](#cite_note-Griffin-27) He was said to be 'despotic, sluggish and stupid'. He was also noted as a former wrestler who spent many a time hunting.[[35]](#cite_note-35) He was painted by [Francisco Goya](/wiki/Francisco_Goya "Francisco Goya") in a number of official court portraits, which numerous art critics have seen as satires on the King's stout vacuity.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

Main article: [Inauguration of Joe Biden](/wiki/Inauguration_of_Joe_Biden "Inauguration of Joe Biden")

[![Photo of Biden raising his right hand, with his left hand placed on a thick Bible](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Biden_oath_of_office.jpg/250px-Biden_oath_of_office.jpg)](/wiki/File:Biden_oath_of_office.jpg)

Biden takes [the oath of office](/wiki/Oath_of_office_of_the_President_of_the_United_States "Oath of office of the President of the United States") administered by [Chief Justice](/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States "Chief Justice of the United States") [John Roberts](/wiki/John_Roberts "John Roberts") at [the Capitol](/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol"), on January 20, 2021.

Biden was inaugurated as the 46th president of the United States on January 20, 2021.[[337]](#cite_note-hunnicutt-347)[[338]](#cite_note-348) At 78, he was then the oldest person to assume the office up to that point.[[k]](#cite_note-350)[[337]](#cite_note-hunnicutt-347)[[340]](#cite_note-351) Biden was the second [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") U.S. president, after [John F. Kennedy](/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy"),[[341]](#cite_note-352)[[342]](#cite_note-353) and the first president elected from the state of [Delaware](/wiki/Delaware "Delaware").[[343]](#cite_note-354) He was also the first person since [George H. W. Bush](/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") to have been both vice president and president,[[344]](#cite_note-355) and the only president to date from the [Silent Generation](/wiki/Silent_Generation "Silent Generation").[[345]](#cite_note-356)[[346]](#cite_note-357) Biden's inauguration was "a muted affair unlike any previous inauguration" due to COVID-19 precautions as well as massively increased security measures because of the [January 6 United States Capitol attack](/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack").[[347]](#cite_note-358)
